conventions.convention: The two-label model has fixed positive inertial masses, no external forces, and a static C² pair potential u(|x₁−x₂|), with separations in an open interval J₀ contained in (0,∞). The reduced coordinate is r=x₁−x₂ and its mass is μ=m₁m₂/(m₁+m₂).

A motion must lie within the prescribed model time window I₀. Global solutions of the autonomous equations are distinguished from model motions on I₀; global coordinate extensions restrict to model motions on I₀.

For nonzero angular momentum, J=|j|>0 and the oriented orthonormal triad satisfies e₃=j/J and e₁×e₂=e₃. The lifted polar angle increases: ρ²θ′=J/μ. Swept area is an oriented polar-sector integral, with rate J/(2μ).

The gravitational potential is u(ρ)=−κ/ρ, normalized without an added constant, with κ=G_N m₁ᵍm₂ᵍ>0. Gravitational couplings and inertial masses remain distinct unless the additional identification mᵢᵍ=mᵢ is explicitly adopted.

The CODATA 2022 assignment for G_N is a qualified estimate, not an exact constant: 6.67430(15)×10⁻¹¹ m³ kg⁻¹ s⁻², relative standard uncertainty 2.2×10⁻⁵. The 16 inputs, unchanged from 2018, receive a 3.9 uncertainty expansion factor. These details agree with [CODATA 2022, Sections XIV and XV.A](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2409.03787).
The conic and period results explicitly assume Countable Choice. Their completeness and periodicity conclusions concern the negative-energy branch with nonzero angular momentum.
Circular-orbit frequency means the frequency of the linearised radial equation at fixed J, requiring (U_eff)″(r₀)>0. No nonlinear stability conclusion is asserted.

All numerical examples use declared exact model data, including their deliberately non-CODATA values of G_N; they report no measurements. Periodicity of absolute label positions additionally requires zero centre-of-mass velocity.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated two-label static central pair-potential model, the evaluated forces are central and antisymmetric, P is constant and X is affine, and r=x₁−x₂ satisfies μr″=−u′(|r|)r/|r|. On the fixed motion interval, x↦(X,r) is a bijection onto affine centre-of-mass curves and central-force trajectories for (μ,u), reconstructed by x₁=X+(m₂/M)r and x₂=X−(m₁/M)r.

Adopt the restricted two-label class with a static C² central pair potential on the collision-excluded domain and no external forces; define its reduced problem, separately adopt the fixed-centre idealization, and fix the reading conventions and exclusions.
For u∈Cᵏ(J₀), k≥1, on an open interval J₀⊆(0,∞), A={x∈R³:|x|∈J₀} is open and excludes zero; N(x)=|x| is smooth with DN(x)h=⟨x,h⟩/|x|; U=u∘N is Cᵏ with ∇U(x)=u′(|x|)x/|x|.

Assuming Countable Choice, a gravitational relative trajectory with J>0 has ρ=p/(1+e cos(θ−θ₀)), p=J²/(μκ), and E=(μκ²/(2J²))(e²−1). It obeys the positive periapsis barrier p/(1+e). For E<0 its relative trajectory extends uniquely to all real time and is periodic, with ellipse semiaxes a=p/(1−e²)=−κ/(2E), b=a√(1−e²), and scaled barycentric ellipses.

For J>0, the radial coordinate satisfies μρ″=−(U_eff_J)′(ρ), with constant E=μρ′²/2+U_eff_J(ρ). Conversely, C² radial data valued in J₀ solving that equation, together with θ′=J/(μρ²), reconstruct a central-force trajectory with angular momentum Je₃ and, with affine centre-of-mass data, a two-label motion.

The relative angular momentum is constant and orthogonal to r and r′. For j≠0, the areal-velocity vector is j/(2μ), the swept-area function has derivative J/(2μ), and the two barycentric areal-velocity vectors are scaled by (m₂/M)² and (m₁/M)².

Assuming Countable Choice, for the negative-energy gravitational relative orbit, T=2πμab/J=2π√(μ/κ)a^(3/2), and T²=4π²μa³/κ. Under mᵢᵍ=mᵢ this becomes T²=4π²a³/(G_N M). Both barycentric positions are T-periodic; absolute label motions are periodic exactly when V=0.

concerns.concern: Facts [L3] states μa³/κ=(3/2)/1.2 · (512/27)×10¹⁸=(64/27)×10¹⁸. The displayed middle expression actually equals (640/27)×10¹⁸. The declared data give μ/κ=0.125, because the powers 10²⁴ and 10²⁵ contribute an additional factor 10⁻¹. The final period and Verification 1.1 use the correct value, but the intermediate equality in [L3] is false.

Counterexample 4.1 concludes that the hypothesis Fᵢ_ext≡0 'is necessary'; the closing Scope remark repeats that the theorem's hypotheses are 'necessary'. The witness proves that unrestricted external forces cannot simply be allowed. It does not prove zero external forces necessary for the relative equation: the item's preceding remark correctly identifies nonzero common external acceleration Fᵢ_ext=mᵢa, which cancels from that equation. The necessity wording overstates the established conclusion.
Facts [L6] calls A⊆R³ an 'open interval'. A is the radial annulus {y:|y|∈J₀}, while J₀ is the open interval. The mathematical argument uses the correct domain elsewhere.

The first Remarks bullet says that 'for a closed orbit traversed once' the polar-sector integral is the enclosed area, then excludes a geometric area identification for possibly self-intersecting orbits. Closedness alone does not supply simplicity or one angular winding. State the additional simple, single-revolution condition for the ordinary enclosed-area identification; the proved constant sector-integral rate is unaffected.

The Radial motion paragraph says 'For j=0 no polar angle ... exist'. Its own subsequent derivation gives r=ρn₀ with constant direction; after choosing a plane containing n₀ this has a constant polar angle. What fails is the nonzero-angular-momentum angular parametrization and the distinguished plane normal j, rather than existence of any polar angle.

alerts.finding: The page summary of ex-cm15-impact-check says 'the elastic case exchanges the velocities' for m₁=2 kg, m₂=6 kg and incoming velocities 3 and −1 m/s. The opened item, Example and Verification 2.1, correctly gives outgoing velocities −3 and +1 m/s: each velocity reverses. Exchanging them would give −1 and +3 m/s and total momentum 16 kg m/s instead of the initial zero.

Clause (i) attributes '[μ]=𝖬' to def-cm01-units. The opened units Definition uses μ as its mass-dimension generator, alongside ℓ and τ; it does not define 𝖬. The reduced mass and its kilogram unit are correct, but the cited dimension symbol is inconsistent with the supplier.

Facts [L3] says 'every x∈Rⁿ' has expansion x=Σⱼ₌₁³⟨x,sⱼ⟩sⱼ. This fact belongs to the stated R³ setting; the three-vector expansion does not hold for arbitrary n. The Statement and actual proof use R³ correctly.

seams_checked.note: The physical transfers preserve positive mass, C² radial potential, collision exclusion, J>0 for polar reduction, E<0 for elliptic completeness, and Countable Choice for ellipse geometry and period.
The centre-of-mass and momentum definitions agree. Momentum balance is invoked after deriving an antisymmetric pair presentation with zero external forces.
The force and potential branches retain their regularity hypotheses and motion notion. Circular and elliptic extensions explicitly respect the prescribed time window.
Fixed positive inertial masses, C² coordinate curves, the unconstrained open configuration domain, point-particle scope and SI dimensions are preserved.

The pairing derivative lemma is used with differentiable curves on nondegenerate intervals. The period supplier's continuation argument supplies compact state trapping and handles both time directions.
The examples retain central-force attached-object conventions and Countable Choice where needed. Their conic computations are conditional model checks, not existence or asymptotic assertions.
Positive inertial masses and SI units are used consistently; the constants are expressly declared model values.
The counterexample's constant external maps satisfy the standing force regularity, and its polynomial curves satisfy the motion equations on the collision-excluded domain.
The counterexample correctly applies momentum balance with zero total external force and obtains an affine centre of mass. The separate overstatement about necessity is recorded in concerns.
Curve differentiation and pairing identities are used within their stated interval and differentiability hypotheses.
ex-cm14-kepler-radial-action-check uses the gravitational reduction and effective potential at fixed J>0, carries Countable Choice, and expressly restricts the radial-period identification to 0<e<1.

The scattering definition and theorems retain the static two-label central class, no external forces and the reduced-coordinate reconstruction. Additional finite-range or repulsive-potential assumptions are supplied locally, and autonomous time-window extension is distinguished.

The zero-potential use is allowed by the central class. Contact examples are explicitly separate impulse or fixed-wall models; they are not presented as consequences of smooth central dynamics. The unrelated incorrect elastic-velocity page summary is routed in alerts.
